spec_match.rationale: The seventeen standard-mapping positions are taken from the Gamepad specification's remapping section, and every interface claim is read from the browser's own prototypes rather than from documentation. The feature's absence is shown as a struck-through member alongside the three that exist.

interactive.rationale: A live interface reader with a controller poll; a seventeen-slot mapping grid that watches a connected controller at animation-frame rate and lights up pressed buttons; and an editable lookup table run against a set of device id strings with a live matched/unmatched count.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index says the problem plainly — seventeen positions have meanings and everything past them is a number — which is the ChromeStatus summary's own framing, and names the controls that actually live out there.

edge_cases.rationale: No controller connected (the normal case for anyone reading this); a controller with no buttons past the standard mapping, which the page says would not benefit; an id string no rule matches; and a near-miss substring, which the comparison table calls out as the failure mode that looks like success.

references.rationale: chromestatus.com/feature/5075054393163776 on the index and all three concept pages, with the Gamepad specification, its remapping section and MDN's GamepadButton.

conformance.rationale: Six immutable assertions: the API and the interface exist; pressed, touched and value are present; type is present (the feature); Gamepad exposes id, mapping and buttons so the workaround is describable; and getGamepads returns a list without a controller, which is what lets every page here probe on a machine with no hardware.

runtime_evidence.rationale: deno task drive over all three pages in real Chrome 150: 3/3, 26 assertions. Fully verified without hardware: GamepadButton has exactly pressed, touched and value and no type, both with and without --enable-experimental-web-platform-features; Gamepad exposes all seven expected members; the mapping grid renders seventeen correctly-labelled positions; and the lookup table matched 3 of 6 device strings, rising to 4 when a rule was added. NOT verified: anything involving a real controller — no gamepad was connected, and the harness has no way to emulate one, so the live paths on all three pages are unexercised.

telemetry_health.rationale: Each page emits showcaseTelemetry.assert with the probed member counts, the number of controllers polled, and the lookup table's match counts.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout, no raw colour literals, buttons set background and colour, 44px control minimums, and the wide tables in their own scroll containers.

accessibility.rationale: The mapping grid states each slot's index and name as text with its state written out rather than shown only by inversion; the absent members are struck through and marked by class as well as colour; tables carry row headers and captions that update; results are announced through aria-live.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: The slot grid is auto-fill minmax(150px) and reflows to a single column at 360px; control grids auto-fit; the device and comparison tables scroll inside their own containers. A gamepad on a phone is unusual but not impossible, and nothing here assumes a pointer.

openQuestions.title: Nothing here has ever seen a controller
openQuestions.detail: All three pages have a live path, and none of it has run: the build machine has no gamepad and the harness cannot emulate one. The mapping grid's pressed state, the poll's id column, and the lookup table's live match are all unexercised code. A single run with a real controller — ideally one with a trackpad or paddles, so the tail is non-empty — would exercise every one of them and is the obvious next step.

openQuestions.title: The device id strings are illustrative and should be labelled harder
openQuestions.detail: The strings in the lookup table demo are the shape real ids take, and the page says so, but a reader in a hurry could take them for a table worth copying. Sourcing a handful of verified id strings — same device across three operating systems — would make the point sharper and would remove the risk of the demo being mistaken for a database.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible live status grid updating at animation frame rate
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Do not announce every frame of a high-frequency update; give the grid text state and announce a summary at a human pace.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The seventeen slots carry their state as text and update in place at 60Hz without being a live region; the aria-live summary beneath them is rewritten every thirty frames rather than every frame, so a screen reader gets a readable cadence instead of a stream.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: deno task drive starts watching, waits, and asserts the summary text — which updates on the throttled path.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive grid of small status cards without horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: auto-fill with an intrinsic minimum so a grid of many small items reflows rather than scrolling sideways.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The mapping grid is repeat(auto-fill, minmax(150px, 1fr)); the control and fact grids are auto-fit; the two wide tables sit in overflow-x:auto wrappers.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: responsive-check desktop + mobile on the feature.

summary: Three concepts about a property that is not here, built so that the parts not needing hardware are fully exercised and the parts that do are clearly marked as unexercised. The strongest page is the lookup table: it makes the maintenance cost countable — 3 of 6 real-shaped device strings matched, 4 after adding a rule — which is a better argument than describing the problem.
